s1.syndrome_frame: Pelvic mass with restricted mobility and primary infertility
salient_findings: Large pelvic mass extending from the right adnexa to the left
Bilateral breast nodules suggestive of fibroadenomas
Cervix not visualized due to large firm mass
key_facts: Patient is a 29-year-old female
Presenting with primary infertility
Large pelvic mass is soft to firm and bosselated
Mass has restricted mobility and extends from pelvis to epigastrium
Bilateral breast nodules are suggestive of fibroadenomas
Serum tumor markers are within normal limits
MRI findings suggest an ovarian primary
Histopathology shows spindle cell tumor with diffuse hemangiopericytomatous pattern of vasculature
Immunohistochemistry shows diffuse positivity for smooth muscle actin (SMA)
Genetic testing detected a pathogenic variant in the FH gene

s4.champion: Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer

raw.champion: Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer
raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a large pelvic mass, primary infertility, and bilateral breast nodules suggestive of fibroadenomas, along with the histopathological findings of a spindle cell tumor and the detection of a pathogenic variant in the FH gene, are all consistent with Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer (HLRCC). The genetic testing result is particularly supportive of this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Uterine leiomyoma
rejected.why: While the patient presents with a large pelvic mass, the mass is described as extending from the right adnexa to the left and is suggestive of an ovarian primary, rather than a uterine origin.

rejected.label: Ovarian leiomyoma
rejected.why: Although the mass is described as an ovarian primary, the presence of a pathogenic variant in the FH gene and the patient's other symptoms are more suggestive of a hereditary condition like HLRCC.

rejected.label: Hemangiopericytoma
rejected.why: While the histopathology shows a diffuse hemangiopericytomatous pattern of vasculature, the overall clinical and genetic picture is more consistent with HLRCC.

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: The patient's tumor markers are within normal limits and the MIB-1 labeling index is low (1-5%), which is not typical for a malignant tumor like leiomyosarcoma.
